title: Azure API Management (APIM) Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.51 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.51 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="GatewayLogs"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.51_azure_api_management_api_51"
| sort -_time
description: APIM is the gateway for API-first architectures. Backend errors, high latency, and rate limit breaches directly impact API consumers and downstream applications.
value: Detecting azure api management (apim) health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable diagnostics on APIM to send GatewayLogs via Event Hub to Splunk. Collect metrics for `Requests`, `BackendDuration`, `OverallDuration`, `FailedRequests`, and `UnauthorizedRequests`. Alert on backend error rate spikes, latency exceeding SLA thresholds, and capacity exhaustion (approaching unit limits). Track API-level usage patterns for capacity planning.
visualization: Line chart (request rate and error rate by API), Gauge (latency vs. SLA), Table (top errors by API and operation).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics) with the modular input for `azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable diagnostics on APIM to send GatewayLogs via Event Hub to Splunk. Collect metrics for `Requests`, `BackendDuration`, `OverallDuration`, `FailedRequests`, and `UnauthorizedRequests`. Alert on backend error rate spikes, latency exceeding SLA thresholds, and capacity exhaustion (approaching unit limits). Track API-level usage patterns for capacity planning.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="GatewayLogs"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.51_azure_api_management_api_51"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:diagnostics` in `index=cloud` to detect azure api management (apim) health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_51_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (request rate and error rate by API), Gauge (latency vs. SLA), Table (top errors by API and operation)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure api management (apim) health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
